title: Efficiently Learning To Reason or Not to Reason: Root-token Policy Optimization for Adaptive Thinking
curriculum: Three stages: original LRM -> SFT for mode selection -> RPO. The SFT loop (Algorithm 1) iteratively refreshes the correctness-filtered self-distilled data and keeps training only while default-template accuracy stays within a tolerance epsilon of the original model; one iteration usually sufficed. SFT is described as a controllability enabler rather than a capability stage, because over-training degrades the solver (R1-Distill-1.5B MATH500 drops 83.2 -> 75.1 after 1 epoch). RPO then runs for fewer than 60 update steps on the balanced easy/hard prompt mix.
eval_metrics: Benchmarks: MATH500, AIME24 and AIME25 for math, plus GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench (2025-03-25 to 2025-04-15) for transfer. Metrics: Pass@1 averaged over 16 runs, average generated tokens, Think% (fraction routed to LONG), and the reasoning-per-accuracy ratio RAR = Think%/Pass@1 (lower is better). Also reported: ECE/MCE reliability diagrams for p_short, a training-compute PFLOPs accounting, and misrouting counts. Qwen3-8B math average: Think% 57.3 -> 44.8 with Pass@1 63.8 -> 62.0 and RAR 0.90 -> 0.72. Exaone4-1.2B RAR 0.85 -> 0.49.
key_results: RPO's training compute is an estimated ~0.02x that of AdaptThink (10,241 vs 522,240 PFLOPs for an 8B model) while it still learns difficulty-aware routing. On R1-1.5B it reaches 51.3 average Pass@1 at 20.5% MATH500 Think% (RAR 0.96) versus AdaptThink's 56.5 (RAR 0.74) at a much larger budget. At an equal ~10K-PFLOP budget, full-trajectory GRPO only reaches 90.2% Think% while RPO reaches 20.5-43.4% at comparable accuracy.
evolution_note: RPO targets the overthinking problem of R1-style LRMs and follows the learn-when-to-think line (AdaptThink, Thinkless, ARM, AdaReasoner), whose full-trajectory GRPO is costly. It takes token-selective RL (high-entropy forking tokens) to its extreme by updating a single root routing token, making adaptive thinking trainable on ~3 GPUs with open data. The authors present it as a controllable routing layer on top of SFT, not a uniform replacement: gains are configuration-dependent (e.g., Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-1.7B show comparable rather than better RAR).
